title: Intel’s new D270 AI chip gives bigger models more room to work
key_facts: Intel shared new details on 12 Oct at the Open Compute Project Global Summit on its GPU D-series; the D270 is a server accelerator for running AI models (inference).
It is the hardware earlier called Crescent Island, first announced in October 2025; customer sampling is under way.
Intel's own card has 160GB of LPDDR5X memory; partners can build cards with up to 480GB.
Intel says it supports models up to 300 billion parameters on one card, or over a trillion across eight.
Memory bandwidth is 1.5 TB/s; it uses the Xe3P architecture, PCIe 5.0, 350 watts and passive air cooling.
No general availability date or pricing was given; supported-model figures are Intel's claims and do not show speed.
quote_evidence: This is the hardware previously called Crescent Island, which Intel first announced in October 2025.
Intel's October announcement doesn't provide general availability or pricing.
why_it_matters_hint: Intel is pitching big memory and air cooling for cheaper AI serving.
